docs.title: Resource Inventory Prompt

docs.text: You are acting as a resource-discovery, scope-definition, and evidence-preparation agent for the SEPIO requirements-collection workflow. Your task is to identify, evaluate, and organize the best available resources for understanding the following project/data/model and then recommend one or more reasonable scopes for a subsequent requirements review. PROJECT [PROJECT NAME] INITIAL PROJECT CONTEXT / SCOPE NOTES [Optional. Insert any initial project description, known canonical distribution, exclusions, questions, or tentative scope notes from the project representative. If nothing is supplied, discover and propose the scope from the available project resources.] GOAL Assemble a proposed Resource Inventory / Evidence Package that another AI agent can later use to complete the SEPIO Requirements Forms accurately and reproducibly. Do not complete the requirements forms yet. Do not map project concepts to SEPIO yet. Do not infer project requirements from what SEPIO supports. A central output of this task is one or more PROVISIONAL SCOPE STATEMENTS that the project representative can review and select before requirements elicitation. IMPORTANT ORDER-OF-OPERATIONS RULE Do NOT author the final provisional scope statements before you have: 1. discovered the relevant project resources; 2. assigned each source a stable Source ID such as S01, S02, S03; 3. classified each source's authority and requirements role; 4. identified representative examples; 5. documented important source conflicts, ambiguities, version issues, and scope exclusions; and 6. identified the recommended current-state canonical source set and broader desired-state evidence set. The scope statements should be written AFTER the Resource Inventory and source classification are established so that they can refer to concrete resources by **Source ID + name/version**. Think of the workflow this way: RESOURCE DISCOVERY ↓ RESOURCE INVENTORY WITH SOURCE IDs ↓ SOURCE ROLE / AUTHORITY CLASSIFICATION ↓ RECOMMENDED CURRENT-STATE AND DESIRED-STATE SOURCE SETS ↓ PROVISIONAL SCOPE STATEMENTS ↓ HUMAN SCOPE SELECTION ↓ REQUIREMENTS FORM COMPLETION The Resource Inventory should make explicit: - which exact source(s), dataset(s), distribution(s), release(s), or companion artifacts should control CURRENT-STATE requirements answers; - which broader project resources may be used to identify DESIRED-STATE requirements; - what resources are context only and must not be used as requirements evidence; - which materials are publicly accessible and should normally be retrieved directly by the later requirements agent; - which materials, if any, require a human project representative to download, upload, or clarify. SCOPE-DESIGN PRINCIPLES 1. Separate current-state scope from desired-state scope. The subsequent requirements forms contain two distinct concepts: CURRENT STATE: What is represented in the selected canonical project source(s) for this review? DESIRED STATE: What should the SEPIO-based representation support, based on the broader, evidence-supported project requirements allowed by the selected scope? Do not assume the same source set must control both. 2. Every provisional scope statement must contain TWO EXPLICIT SUBSECTIONS. Each proposed scope must be structured with at least: ### Current-state canonical scope This subsection must state: - what project/data product is being assessed for current state; - the exact Source IDs + source names/versions that control current-state / F1 / "Used in Current Data?" answers; - any explicitly designated canonical companion artifacts; - what kinds of related resources are excluded from current-state reasoning. Use language such as: "Current-state/F1 answers must be based only on S05 — [source name/version] and S06 — [source name/version]. No other resource may change an F1 answer unless the scope is revised." The later requirements agent must strictly stick to this set for current-state answers. 3. Every provisional scope statement must also contain: ### Desired-state scope This subsection must state: - what broader project capabilities are in scope for desired-state/F2 requirements; - the exact Source IDs + source names/versions that may inform desired state; - whether each broader source is being used as: - EXPLICIT_FUTURE_REQUIREMENT - EXISTING_PROJECT_CAPABILITY_NOT_IN_CANONICAL_EXPORT - DOCUMENTED_MODEL_INTENT - important exclusions from desired-state reasoning; - the rule that any F2 answer that differs from F1 must identify its supporting source in `Explanation / Considerations`. Use language such as: "Desired-state/F2 answers may additionally draw on S01 — [paper], S08 — [intermediate artifact], and S09 — [alignment/QC artifact] to identify a maximal, evidence-supported requirements set. When F2 differs from F1, the requirements agent must identify the supporting source and support type in `Explanation / Considerations`." 4. The CURRENT-STATE CANONICAL SOURCE SET must be precise and reproducible. This is the exact set of source(s), dataset(s), distribution(s), release(s), or explicitly designated companion artifacts that the later requirements agent must use to populate current-state / "Used in Current Data?" columns. Examples: - one versioned `indications.xlsx` distribution; - one current LinkML schema release plus explicitly designated canonical example data; - one KG release artifact; - one database export and its required schema/data dictionary. Do not broaden current state simply because richer information exists elsewhere in the project. 5. The DESIRED-STATE EVIDENCE SET may be broader. When relevant and not explicitly out of scope, desired-state evidence may include: - explicit future requirements or roadmaps; - current project/model documentation and papers; - intermediate curation/analysis artifacts; - data captured elsewhere in the project pipeline but dropped from the canonical export; - alternate or earlier project distributions; - other project-maintained representations; - competency questions; - curation guidance; - implementation/design documents. The purpose is to support an initial MAXIMAL EVIDENCE-SUPPORTED requirements set that a human reviewer can later narrow. "Maximal" does not mean speculative. Every desired-state capability must be supported by project-specific evidence. 6. Classify desired-state support where useful. Use these labels when characterizing why a noncanonical resource is informative for desired state: - EXPLICIT_FUTURE_REQUIREMENT A roadmap, issue, requirements document, competency question, or explicit statement says the project wants/needs the capability. - EXISTING_PROJECT_CAPABILITY_NOT_IN_CANONICAL_EXPORT The project already captures or uses the information in an intermediate artifact, alternate distribution, curation workflow, analysis product, or other project-maintained representation, but it is absent from the proposed canonical current-state distribution. - DOCUMENTED_MODEL_INTENT A paper, model/design document, curation guide, or other authoritative project document describes the capability as part of the intended project model/data product, even if absent from the proposed canonical current-state source. 7. Do not use a source as desired-state evidence when it explicitly says the capability is out of scope, rejected, deprecated, or intentionally excluded, unless another authoritative project source explicitly reverses that decision. SOURCE-DISCOVERY RULES 8. Respect supplied project context and discover scope boundaries. Distinguish the scoped project/data product from: - upstream source databases; - internal systems that are outside scope; - downstream APIs; - user-interface/display enrichments; - unrelated derived exports; - historical/superseded project versions. For every source, consider whether it describes: - the canonical project/data model itself; - a candidate canonical current-state distribution; - an alternate or historical project representation; - an intermediate curation/analysis artifact; - an upstream source; - a downstream representation; - an implementation detail; - future/project intent. 9. Prefer current, authoritative sources, but do not discard older/alternate/intermediate project artifacts that may legitimately inform desired state. For CURRENT-STATE canonical-source recommendations, prioritize: a. current authoritative schema/data model; b. current canonical distribution/release; c. current authoritative data dictionary; d. current representative data/examples; e. explicitly designated canonical companion artifacts. For DESIRED-STATE evidence, also consider: f. current model/design documentation and papers; g. current curation/evidence/provenance guidance; h. current ingest/transformation/pipeline artifacts; i. explicit requirements, competency questions, roadmap documents, or issues; j. intermediate curation/analysis artifacts; k. alternate or earlier project distributions that expose project capabilities or intent. When sources conflict: - identify the conflict; - state which source should control current state; - explain whether the conflicting resource remains useful for desired-state evidence; - do not silently reconcile the difference. 10. Look for sources that can answer questions about: - the kinds of claims/associations/statements represented; - how claims are structurally packaged; - whether claims are represented as reified objects, direct graph edges, slot/value pairs, tabular records, or other forms; - how subject, relationship/predicate, object, and qualifiers are represented; - what kinds of evidence items are retained or referenced; - whether evidence items are represented locally, externally, or both; - whether evidence direction, strength, grouping, or higher-order synthesis is represented; - confidence or scoring information; - provenance about agents, methods, resources, dates, review, extraction, grounding, normalization, encoding, retrieval, or ingest; - what information is retained from upstream sources versus discarded or transformed; - what richer information is captured in intermediate project artifacts but lost in the canonical distribution; - current capabilities versus documented future/intended requirements. 11. Include representative data/examples. When possible, identify a small but diverse set of examples that covers the major claim and EPC patterns. Include examples from: - candidate canonical current-state sources; and - broader desired-state sources when they reveal additional project requirements. Prefer examples that collectively test different situations, such as: - a claim with publication or regulatory support; - a claim with structured evidence metadata; - a claim with qualifiers/context; - a claim with source/provenance but little explicit evidence; - a case where richer project-internal EPC is dropped from the canonical export; - a case involving normalization/transformation; - an alternate distribution exposing a capability absent from the canonical one; - any unusual but important pattern. Do not collect large datasets when a small representative sample will establish the relevant structure and semantics. Assign each representative example a stable ID such as E01, E02, E03. 12. Record precise source locations and source roles BEFORE writing the scope statements. Assign each source a stable ID such as S01, S02, S03. For each source, record: - Source ID - Source title/name - Source type - URL or repository path - Repository/release/tag/commit/version when available - Authority level - Requirements role - Desired-state support type, when applicable - Scope relevance - Requirement dimensions supported - Important directly observed facts - Access status - Whether the later requirements agent should retrieve it directly or human assistance may be required - Notes/cautions Use these authority labels where appropriate: - PRIMARY_AUTHORITATIVE - SUPPORTING_CURRENT - REPRESENTATIVE_EXAMPLE - HISTORICAL_BACKGROUND - OUT_OF_SCOPE_CONTEXT Use these REQUIREMENTS ROLE labels: - CURRENT_STATE_CANONICAL - CURRENT_STATE_CANONICAL_COMPANION - DESIRED_STATE_SUPPORT - CURRENT_AND_DESIRED - CONTEXT_ONLY A source should receive CURRENT_STATE_CANONICAL or CURRENT_STATE_CANONICAL_COMPANION only if you recommend that the later requirements agent be allowed to use it for current-state answers under at least one proposed scope. 13. Capture directly observed facts from key sources. For each major authoritative source, record concise facts explicitly supported by the source. Examples: - "The canonical table contains subject ID, object ID, and a source-text field." - "The canonical record does not contain evidence-direction or evidence-strength fields." - "Intermediate curation records retain Name Resolver candidates and LLM QC outcomes, but the final export drops them." - "The project paper describes hyperrelations absent from the selected release." Distinguish these directly observed facts from interpretation. Use labels where helpful: - DIRECT - INFERRED - UNRESOLVED 14. Retrieve publicly accessible materials before asking the human to provide them. When a potentially important source is publicly accessible: - first attempt to access/download it yourself; - follow GitHub, DOI/archive, release, and direct-download links; - inspect actual files/artifacts when record-level or schema-level details matter. Human assistance is a fallback, not the default. 15. Identify inaccessible, ambiguous, or human-supplied materials precisely. Human intervention may be needed when: - the agent cannot access/download the resource; - authentication, institutional permission, or a private repository is required; - the source exists only locally/internally; - multiple plausible files/versions exist and the canonical one cannot be identified confidently; - the public copy is stale/incomplete and the representative may have a better copy; - a human decision is required to choose the canonical source/version or scope. If human assistance is needed: - identify the exact file/resource; - provide the URL/path when known; - explain why it matters; - state what question it is needed to answer; - state whether discovery/requirements elicitation can proceed provisionally without it; - tell the project representative exactly what to download, upload, or clarify. 16. Distinguish process documentation from stored project content. A project may document curation, extraction, review, normalization, mapping, evidence assessment, encoding, or transformation. For each such source, determine whether it shows: - information actually stored in the proposed canonical current-state source; - information captured elsewhere by the project but omitted from the canonical export; - only an implementation process with no evidence that its outputs are retained. This distinction is especially important for desired-state scope design. 17. Do not begin filling the SEPIO Requirements Forms until the Resource Inventory has been reviewed and one project scope statement has been selected, or the project representative explicitly authorizes the requirements agent to use the recommended scope. PROVISIONAL SCOPE STATEMENTS 18. Author provisional scope statements ONLY AFTER the Resource Inventory and recommended source sets have been completed. The scope statements should function as selections over the Resource Inventory. Do not write vague statements such as: "Use the current dataset and relevant documentation." Instead write: "Use S05 — `matrix_indication_list.xlsx`, v1.3.0 and S06 — `matrix_contraindication_list.xlsx`, v1.3.0 for current state. Desired state may additionally use S01 — MeDIC primary publication and S09 — FDA semantic-alignment/QC intermediates..." Every named resource should be identifiable from the Resource Inventory by Source ID and name/version. 19. At minimum, provide: SCOPE A — MINIMAL / CANONICAL-DISTRIBUTION-ONLY This scope should: - identify the narrowest defensible CURRENT-STATE CANONICAL SOURCE SET; - restrict current-state answers to those canonical source(s); - normally restrict desired-state answers to the same canonical source(s), unless a small number of explicitly inseparable canonical companion artifacts are required; - produce a conservative requirements record describing the canonical distribution itself. Structure it as: ### Current-state canonical scope - Scope statement - Sources: Sxx — [name/version], Syy — [name/version] - Explicit exclusions ### Desired-state scope - Scope statement - Sources: usually the same source set for the minimal option - Explicit exclusions ### Strengths / tradeoffs 20. Also provide: SCOPE B — MAXIMAL / CANONICAL CURRENT STATE + BROAD DESIRED STATE This scope should: - identify the exact CURRENT-STATE CANONICAL SOURCE SET; - require the later agent to use only that set for current-state/F1 answers; - identify a broader DESIRED-STATE EVIDENCE SET; - allow desired-state/F2 answers to draw on project-specific evidence such as: - intermediate curation/analysis artifacts; - alternate/earlier project distributions; - other maintained project outputs; - authoritative papers/documentation; - curation/modeling guidance; - roadmaps/issues/explicit requirements; - aim for a maximal evidence-supported desired-state requirements set that the human reviewer can later whittle down; - require the requirements agent to name the desired-state supporting source in `Explanation / Considerations` whenever F2 differs from F1. Structure it as: ### Current-state canonical scope - Scope statement - Exact Source IDs + names/versions - Canonical companions, if any - Explicit exclusions - Rule that no noncanonical source may change F1 unless the scope is revised ### Desired-state scope - Scope statement - Exact Source IDs + names/versions - Desired-state support type for each broader source - Explicit exclusions - Rule that F2 differences must cite supporting source + support type in `Explanation / Considerations` ### Strengths / tradeoffs 21. If other reasonable project scopes emerge, provide additional alternatives such as: - CURRENT RELEASE + CURRENT PIPELINE ARTIFACTS; - CORE PRODUCT + DESIGNATED COMPANION DATASETS; - DOMAIN-SPECIFIC SUBSET; - STRICT HISTORICAL RELEASE; - CURRENT PRODUCT FAMILY / MULTI-DISTRIBUTION SCOPE. Every additional scope must use the same explicit two-part structure: ### Current-state canonical scope ### Desired-state scope 22. Recommend one scope. After presenting alternatives: - identify the scope you recommend for the initial requirements exercise; - explain why; - state the tradeoff between reproducibility/conservatism and broader requirements discovery. Unless project context argues otherwise, prefer recommending the MAXIMAL scope for the initial requirements pass because it preserves a strict canonical basis for current state while surfacing a broader evidence-supported desired-state requirements set for human review. DELIVERABLE Return a Markdown document named: [PROJECT_NAME]_Resource_Inventory.md IMPORTANT: Use the following section order. The Resource Inventory and source classification must appear BEFORE the provisional scope statements so that the scope can reference established Source IDs. A. Project context used Restate the supplied project context/scope notes and any important assumptions used during discovery. B. Resource inventory Provide a table with these columns: - Source ID - Name - Type - URL / repository path - Version / release / commit - Authority level - Requirements role - Desired-state support type - Requirement dimensions supported - Important directly observed facts - Access status - Retrieval / human-assistance guidance - Notes / cautions For Desired-state support type, use when applicable: - EXPLICIT_FUTURE_REQUIREMENT - EXISTING_PROJECT_CAPABILITY_NOT_IN_CANONICAL_EXPORT - DOCUMENTED_MODEL_INTENT - N/A For Access status, use concise values where possible: - PUBLIC_ACCESSIBLE - PUBLIC_DOWNLOADABLE - ACCESS_NOT_VERIFIED - ACCESS_FAILED - AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED - PRIVATE_OR_LOCAL - CANONICAL_FILE_AMBIGUOUS For Retrieval / human-assistance guidance, use: - AGENT_RETRIEVE - HUMAN_PROVIDE_IF_AGENT_ACCESS_FAILS - HUMAN_PROVIDE_REQUIRED - HUMAN_CONFIRM_CANONICAL_VERSION - HUMAN_CONFIRM_SCOPE - CONTEXT_ONLY_NO_DOWNLOAD_NEEDED C. Representative data/examples List selected examples using stable IDs. For each: - Example ID - Current-state or desired-state example - Source ID + source name - Claim/record type - EPC/model pattern demonstrated - Why selected - Whether directly inspected or still needs retrieval Prefer examples from both: - canonical current-state sources; - broader desired-state sources that reveal additional requirements. D. Upstream/downstream/context resources that should NOT be treated as canonical requirements evidence List neighboring systems/resources that could cause scope confusion. Explain whether each is: - context only; - allowed only as desired-state evidence under a specific scope; - fully out of scope. E. Known source conflicts, ambiguities, or version concerns Document: - conflicting sources; - stale documentation; - unclear implementation behavior; - unresolved version questions; - differences between canonical distribution and richer intermediate/alternate representations; - uncertainty about which release/file is canonical. For each conflict: - state what controls current state; - state whether another source may still inform desired state. F. Recommended source sets Complete this section BEFORE authoring provisional scope statements. ### F1. Recommended current-state canonical source set Identify the exact sources that should control F1/current-state answers under the scope you expect to recommend. For each source: - provide Source ID + source name/version; - explain why it is canonical; - identify any canonical companion artifact that must be interpreted together with it; - state what it is allowed to establish for current state. ### F2. Recommended desired-state evidence set Identify broader sources that may inform F2/desired-state requirements under a maximal scope. For each: - provide Source ID + source name/version; - state why it is relevant; - assign one of: - EXPLICIT_FUTURE_REQUIREMENT - EXISTING_PROJECT_CAPABILITY_NOT_IN_CANONICAL_EXPORT - DOCUMENTED_MODEL_INTENT - note limitations or caveats. ### F3. Sources excluded from requirements evidence List Source IDs that should remain context only or fully out of scope, with a brief reason. G. Provisional scope statements Now author the provisional scopes using the Resource Inventory IDs established above. ### Scope A — Minimal / canonical-distribution-only #### Current-state canonical scope Provide: - paste-ready scope text; - exact Source IDs + names/versions controlling F1; - canonical companions, if any; - explicit exclusions. #### Desired-state scope Provide: - paste-ready scope text; - exact Source IDs + names/versions controlling F2; - explicit exclusions. #### Strengths / tradeoffs ### Scope B — Maximal / canonical current state + broad desired state #### Current-state canonical scope Provide: - paste-ready scope text; - exact Source IDs + names/versions controlling F1; - canonical companions, if any; - explicit exclusions; - explicit statement that noncanonical resources may not change F1 answers. #### Desired-state scope Provide: - paste-ready scope text; - exact Source IDs + names/versions allowed for F2; - desired-state support type for each broader source; - explicit exclusions; - explicit statement that whenever F2 differs from F1, the requirements agent must identify the supporting source + support type in `Explanation / Considerations`. #### Strengths / tradeoffs ### Additional reasonable scope alternatives Include only when justified. Use the same explicit two-part structure: - Current-state canonical scope - Desired-state scope ### Recommended scope State which scope you recommend and why. H. Materials the requirements agent should retrieve vs. materials a human may need to provide Start with this rule: The requirements-completion agent should first attempt to retrieve all publicly accessible materials itself. The project representative should not need to manually download and upload public resources merely because they are listed in the Resource Inventory. Then provide: ### H1. Materials the requirements agent should retrieve directly For each: - Source ID - exact resource/file - URL/path - why needed - what should be inspected ### H2. Materials a human may need to provide only if agent retrieval fails For each: - Source ID - exact resource - why it matters - what the human should upload if requested Do not ask the human to provide these preemptively. ### H3. Materials that genuinely require human provision or clarification List only resources that: - are private/local; - require authentication; - cannot be publicly accessed; - require a human canonical-version decision; - require a human scope-selection decision. If none: "None identified at this stage." I. Evidence gaps / unresolved questions For each unresolved question, indicate whether it: - can likely be resolved by retrieving a public source; - requires human-provided material; - requires a human semantic/project decision; - requires scope selection; - can remain unresolved during preliminary requirements elicitation. J. Recommended handoff for requirements elicitation End with a compact machine-readable block. Use this structure: RECOMMENDED SCOPE: - Scope B — Maximal / canonical current state + broad desired state CURRENT-STATE CANONICAL SOURCES: - S01: [name/version] - S02: [name/version] CURRENT-STATE CANONICAL COMPANIONS: - S03: [name/version] DESIRED-STATE SUPPORT SOURCES: - S04: EXISTING_PROJECT_CAPABILITY_NOT_IN_CANONICAL_EXPORT — [name/version] - S05: DOCUMENTED_MODEL_INTENT — [name/version] - S06: EXPLICIT_FUTURE_REQUIREMENT — [name/version] REPRESENTATIVE EXAMPLES: - E01 - E02 - E03 CONTEXT ONLY / DO NOT USE AS REQUIREMENTS EVIDENCE: - S08 - S09 AGENT SHOULD RETRIEVE DURING REQUIREMENTS REVIEW: - S02: [specific file/artifact] - S04: [specific file/artifact] HUMAN PROVIDE ONLY IF AGENT RETRIEVAL FAILS: - S07: [specific file/artifact] HUMAN-PROVIDED MATERIAL REQUIRED: - NONE or - [specific resource and why] HUMAN CONFIRMATION REQUIRED: - Select/approve one provisional scope before final requirements completion - [other issue] UNRESOLVED: - [brief issue] HANDOFF INSTRUCTION: Use only CURRENT-STATE CANONICAL SOURCES and explicitly designated CURRENT-STATE CANONICAL COMPANIONS to populate F1/current-state requirements. Use the DESIRED-STATE SUPPORT SOURCES allowed by the selected scope to populate an evidence-supported maximal F2/desired-state requirements set. When F2 differs from F1, identify the supporting Source ID + source name and desired-state support type in the form's `Explanation / Considerations` field. Do not use CONTEXT ONLY sources as requirements evidence. Attempt to retrieve public resources before asking the project representative to upload them. Flag unresolved issues for human review rather than guessing. K. Short resource-discovery summary Conclude with 5–10 bullets summarizing: - the canonical model/data product identified; - the recommended current-state canonical source set; - the broader desired-state evidence set; - the recommended scope; - the main EPC patterns observed; - important scope exclusions; - critical source/version conflicts; - additional public materials the requirements agent should retrieve; - whether any material currently requires human provision; - whether the package is ready for scope selection and requirements elicitation.
docs.title: Copyable prompt

docs.text: The Resource Inventory should make the division of responsibility explicit: Public and accessible: the requirements agent retrieves it. Public but retrieval may fail: the human provides it only if the agent asks. Private/local/authenticated: the human provides access or uploads it. Canonical version ambiguous: the human decides which version is authoritative. Scope alternatives remain: the human selects/approves the scope before final requirements completion.
docs.title: Human handoff principle

docs.text: The discovery agent proposes the scope; the project representative owns the scope decision. The important architectural rule is: The Resource Inventory defines the evidence catalog; the scope statement selects which catalog entries control current state and which may inform desired state. For most initial requirements exercises, the recommended default is: strict canonical current state + maximal evidence-supported desired state This gives the modeling workflow a conservative, reproducible account of what the selected canonical distribution represents today while exposing a broader set of project-supported capabilities for human review before SEPIO modeling.
docs.title: Scope-selection principle

docs.text: The completed [PROJECT_NAME]_Resource_Inventory.md is intended to be provided to the requirements-completion agent alongside: Requirements_Collection_Forms.xlsx Requirements_Instructions_and_Guidance_for_AI.md the selected project scope statement any materials explicitly identified as genuinely requiring human provision The selected scope statement should be copied from or derived directly from the Resource Inventory and should preserve its Source IDs. The later requirements agent should attempt to retrieve all other publicly accessible resources itself. The Requirement→SEPIO mapping registry is intentionally not used during resource discovery or requirements elicitation.
docs.title: Relationship to the requirements-form workflow

docs.text: SEPIO Requirements Collection — Project Representative Overview Audience: Project representatives who are asking an AI agent to complete the SEPIO Requirements Forms for their project 1. What this process is for The SEPIO Requirements Forms describe what a biomedical knowledge project currently represents and what it should support about claims, evidence, interpretation, and provenance. The goal is not to redesign your project or force it into SEPIO while the forms are being completed. Instead, the process asks two related questions: Current state: What does the selected canonical source, dataset, distribution, or model actually represent now? Desired state: What broader capabilities does project-specific evidence support as requirements for a future SEPIO-based representation? This distinction is important. Current-state answers should be conservative and reproducible: they are grounded only in the canonical source set explicitly selected for the review. Desired-state answers may use a broader set of project evidence to identify a maximal, evidence-supported requirements set that a human reviewer can later refine or narrow. After the forms are reviewed and confirmed, a separate SEPIO requirements-to-model workflow can use them to: identify relevant SEPIO classes and attributes; generate a candidate project-specific SEPIO covering model; identify partial SEPIO coverage; identify model gaps or extension needs; generate implementation guidance; and identify questions requiring project or SEPIO modeler review. The completed forms are therefore a description of your project's requirements , not a list of SEPIO features you have chosen. 2. What is in this starter package This folder contains: START_HERE.md — a short orientation and five-step entry point. Requirements_Collection_Overview.md — this comprehensive overview of the requirements-collection workflow. Requirements_Collection_Forms.xlsx — the empty requirements workbook the agent should complete. Requirements_Instructions_and_Guidance_for_AI.md — detailed semantic and field-by-field instructions intended primarily for the AI agent. REQUIREMENTS_FORM_PROMPT.md — the ready-to-copy prompt for tasking an agent to complete the requirements workbook. RESOURCE_INVENTORY_PROMPT.md — an optional agent prompt for discovering, classifying, and organizing project resources and proposing candidate scope statements. RESOURCE_INVENTORY_GUIDANCE.md — practical guidance for assembling and reviewing a Resource Inventory. PROJECT_SOURCE_CHECKLIST.md — a checklist for gathering project schemas, documentation, examples, and other evidence. examples/example_scope_statement.md — example project scope statements. examples/example_completed_requirements_review.md — an example Requirements Review Memo. CONTENTS.md — a list of files included in the package. These files are designed to stay together in one directory in the repository. 3. The five-step workflow At a high level: Define the scope. Decide what canonical source(s) control current-state answers and what broader evidence may inform desired-state requirements. Create a Resource Inventory. Identify the best sources, examples, versions, conflicts, access needs, and candidate scope statements. Give the agent the scope, inventory, forms, guidance, and needed resources; have it populate the Requirements Forms. Inspect the completed workbook and Requirements Review Memo. Resolve uncertainties and correct anything that does not accurately reflect the project. Move to SEPIO mapping. Once confirmed, use the requirements record as input to the separate requirements-to-model workflow. The remainder of this document explains each part in more detail. 4. Step 1 — Define the project scope Before asking the requirements agent to populate the forms, define a project scope statement . Biomedical projects often have several related representations: an internal curation model; a canonical public distribution; intermediate curation or analysis artifacts; one or more source databases; an ingest/transformation pipeline; alternate or historical releases; an API representation; a knowledge-graph export; a user-interface representation. Without an explicit scope, an agent can easily mix these together and produce answers that are neither reproducible nor clearly interpretable. A useful scope statement identifies two evidence sets. 4.1 Current-state canonical source set This is the exact source, dataset, distribution, release, schema, or explicitly designated companion artifact that controls the workbook's current-state / “Used in Current Data?” answers. The requirements agent should strictly use only this source set when populating current-state columns. Examples include: one versioned indications.xlsx distribution; one current LinkML schema release plus designated canonical example records; one KG release/export; one production database schema plus its canonical data dictionary. The fact that richer information exists elsewhere in the project does not make it part of current state unless the scope explicitly includes that resource in the canonical source set. 4.2 Desired-state evidence set This is the broader set of project-specific resources the agent is allowed to use when deciding what the future SEPIO-based representation should support. Depending on the selected scope, this can include: explicit future requirements or roadmap items; current papers and project documentation; model/design documentation; intermediate curation or analysis artifacts; information captured elsewhere in the project pipeline but dropped from the canonical export; alternate or earlier project distributions; competency questions; curation guidance; implementation/design documents. The desired-state evidence set supports a maximal but evidence-supported first-pass requirements record. “Maximal” does not mean speculative: every desired-state Y/M answer should still have project-specific support. 4.3 Minimal versus maximal scope The Resource Inventory workflow is designed to propose at least two reasonable scope choices. Minimal / canonical-distribution-only A minimal scope limits the review to one canonical source set. Example: Current-state canonical source: MeDIC matrix_indication_list.xlsx , version 1.3.0. Current-state and desired-state requirements should both be limited to information represented in this canonical distribution. This produces a conservative description of one concrete release. Maximal / canonical current state + broad desired state A maximal scope preserves a strict current-state source while allowing broader project evidence to inform desired state. Example: Current-state canonical source: MeDIC matrix_indication_list.xlsx , version 1.3.0. Current-state answers must be based only on this distribution. Desired-state evidence: additional MeDIC-maintained intermediate curation artifacts, alternate distributions, the MeDIC paper and project documentation, and explicit project requirements may be used to identify a broader, evidence-supported desired-state requirements set. Where desired state differs from current state, the supporting source must be named in Explanation / Considerations . This is often the preferred starting point because it gives a reproducible account of current representation while surfacing a broader set of requirements for human review. 4.4 Other reasonable scopes Some projects may justify additional alternatives, for example: current release + current pipeline artifacts; core product + designated companion datasets; domain-specific subset; strict historical release; current product family / multi-distribution scope. If substantially different products have different evidence/provenance behavior, separate requirements reviews may be clearer. 4.5 How to obtain a scope statement If the scope is already obvious, write it directly. If not, use RESOURCE_INVENTORY_PROMPT.md . The resource-discovery agent should produce: a minimal scope; a maximal scope; additional reasonable alternatives when appropriate; and a recommended scope with tradeoffs. The project representative should review or refine the proposed scope and place the selected statement into the SELECTED PROJECT SCOPE section of REQUIREMENTS_FORM_PROMPT.md . 5. Step 2 — Create a Resource Inventory A Resource Inventory is a structured evidence package for the requirements review. It is more than a list of files. It should tell the later requirements agent: which resources are canonical for current state; which resources may inform desired state; which examples should be inspected; which sources are historical, upstream, downstream, or context only; which versions/releases should be used; what source conflicts or uncertainties exist; which public resources the agent should retrieve itself; which materials may require human provision or clarification. Use RESOURCE_INVENTORY_GUIDANCE.md for detailed guidance. 5.1 Two ways to create the inventory Option A — Assemble it yourself. If you already know the key schema, canonical distribution, documentation, examples, curation guidance, and provenance materials, create a simple inventory or manifest with precise pointers to them. Option B — Ask an AI agent to take a first pass. Use RESOURCE_INVENTORY_PROMPT.md when project evidence is distributed across repositories, documentation sites, papers, DOI archives, generated artifacts, or multiple versions. The agent-generated Resource Inventory should be reviewed before requirements completion. 5.2 Resource roles The inventory should distinguish source roles such as: CURRENT_STATE_CANONICAL CURRENT_STATE_CANONICAL_COMPANION DESIRED_STATE_SUPPORT CURRENT_AND_DESIRED CONTEXT_ONLY Only sources designated as current-state canonical or canonical companions should control current-state answers under the selected scope. 5.3 Desired-state support types When a broader source supports desired state, it is useful to distinguish why: EXPLICIT_FUTURE_REQUIREMENT A roadmap, issue, requirements document, competency question, or explicit project statement says the capability is wanted or needed. EXISTING_PROJECT_CAPABILITY_NOT_IN_CANONICAL_EXPORT The project already captures or uses the information in an intermediate artifact, alternate distribution, curation workflow, analysis product, or other project-maintained representation, but the selected canonical distribution does not expose it. DOCUMENTED_MODEL_INTENT A paper, model/design document, curation guide, or other authoritative project document describes the capability as part of the intended project model or data product, even though it is absent from the selected canonical source. A source that explicitly says a capability is out of scope, rejected, deprecated, or intentionally excluded should not normally be used to justify desired state unless another authoritative project source explicitly reverses that decision. 5.4 Useful resources Typical resources include: Resource type Why it helps Canonical dataset/distribution Establishes what is actually represented in current state. Authoritative schema or data model Shows entities, relationships, fields, structure, and constraints. Data dictionary / field documentation Explains field meaning, allowed values, cardinality, and intended use. Model/design documentation Explains why structures exist and what the project intends to represent. Representative example records Shows how the model is actually used in practice. Intermediate curation/analysis artifacts May reveal existing project capabilities omitted from the canonical export. Source/ingest documentation Shows which upstream information is retained, transformed, or discarded. Curation guidelines / SOPs Helps interpret claims, evidence evaluation, confidence, review, and provenance. Pipeline / normalization documentation Helps identify semantic-alignment and process provenance. Project papers / overview documents Provides project goals, intended semantics, and model intent. Requirements / competency questions / roadmap Captures desired capabilities not yet fully implemented. You do not need every resource type. The goal is to assemble enough evidence to answer each form question responsibly. 5.5 Representative examples The inventory should identify a small, diverse set of examples rather than hundreds of repetitive records. Useful examples may include: a typical claim; a claim with qualifiers/context; a claim with source or evidence support; a claim with richer provenance; a normalization or transformation example; a case where intermediate information is dropped from the canonical export; an alternate distribution that exposes a capability absent from the canonical one. Assign stable IDs such as E01 , E02 , and E03 . 5.6 Public resources and human uploads Public resources are retrieval tasks for the AI agent, not preemptive upload tasks for the project representative. The requirements agent should first try to retrieve public materials itself. Human assistance is appropriate when: public retrieval fails; authentication/private access is required; a source exists only locally; multiple plausible versions/files exist and the canonical one cannot be identified confidently; a human scope or canonical-version decision is required. If human help is needed, the agent should say exactly what resource is needed, why it matters, and whether the review can proceed provisionally without it. 6. Step 3 — Give the agent what it needs and populate the forms Give the requirements agent: REQUIREMENTS_FORM_PROMPT.md the selected project scope statement Requirements_Collection_Forms.xlsx Requirements_Instructions_and_Guidance_for_AI.md the reviewed [PROJECT]_Resource_Inventory.md any private/local materials identified as necessary For the forms and guidance, you may either upload the files or provide links/pointers to the exact versions you want used. For project evidence, you may: upload local files; provide public repository/documentation/DOI links; provide a manifest or Resource Inventory with precise pointers; point to specific files/directories rather than entire repositories. For large datasets, representative records plus structural documentation may be enough unless the agent needs the full dataset to answer a specific requirement. 6.1 Current-state rule For every current-state/F1 answer, the agent should ask: Is this capability represented in the selected current-state canonical source set ? It should not mark something current merely because it appears in: an intermediate artifact; a historical or alternate distribution; a paper; a roadmap; an upstream source; a downstream API/UI; process documentation; unless the selected scope explicitly includes that resource in the current-state canonical source set. 6.2 Desired-state rule For every desired-state/F2 answer, the agent should ask: Is this capability supported as a project requirement by one or more resources allowed in the selected desired-state evidence set? The initial desired-state pass should generally be maximal but evidence-supported . When desired state differs from current state, the agent should identify the supporting source in Explanation / Considerations . A useful pattern is: Current state: [brief observation from canonical source]. Desired-state support: [SUPPORT TYPE] — [Source ID/title/version]: [brief evidence and rationale]. 6.3 How the agent should reason The agent should triangulate across: Selected project scope + Current-state canonical source set + Broader desired-state evidence set + Representative records/examples + Curation / pipeline / provenance documentation + Known requirements / use cases For each substantive answer, it should be able to answer: What project evidence supports this answer, and is that source allowed to support current state, desired state, or both? If that cannot be answered, the response should be marked uncertain rather than guessed. 6.4 Important distinctions to preserve Current representation vs desired requirement A capability may be absent from the canonical current-state distribution but still be a valid desired-state requirement. Upstream source capability vs project capability If an upstream source contains rich EPC information that the project neither stores nor explicitly requires, it should not automatically become a project requirement. Canonical distribution vs intermediate project capability An intermediate project artifact may contain information omitted from the canonical export. Under a maximal scope, this can support desired state as EXISTING_PROJECT_CAPABILITY_NOT_IN_CANONICAL_EXPORT without changing the current-state answer. Canonical model vs downstream API/UI enrichment Downstream computation or display enrichment should not be treated as current canonical representation unless explicitly included in scope. Claim semantics vs evidence/provenance A project may support many biomedical claim types while using one relatively simple evidence/provenance envelope. Assess these dimensions separately. Evidence item vs evidence interpretation A publication, source passage, dataset, or experimental result is not the same thing as an interpreted argument about whether evidence supports or disputes a proposition. Scientific evidence strength vs extraction/alignment confidence A score indicating confidence in entity normalization or extraction should not be treated as scientific evidence strength unless project semantics explicitly say so. Process documentation vs stored provenance Documentation that an LLM, normalization service, curator, or pipeline step was used does not prove that provenance about that process is stored in the canonical data. Missing information vs negative requirement Silence is not automatically “N.” Use M / Maybe / Needs discussion or another review flag when evidence is insufficient. 6.5 Requirements-first rule The Requirement→SEPIO mapping registry should not be used to decide what the project's requirements are. The agent should determine project requirements independently of current SEPIO coverage. 7. Step 4 — Inspect the deliverables The requirements agent should return two primary artifacts. A. Completed Requirements Workbook The agent should populate the provided Requirements_Collection_Forms.xlsx template while preserving its existing structure and formatting. The output filename should include project name, version, date, and 24-hour time, for example: MeDIC_Requirements_v0.2_20261013_1643.xlsx The HHMM form avoids filename problems caused by colons on some operating systems. B. Requirements Review Memo The memo filename should follow the same version/date/time convention, for example: MeDIC_Requirements_Review_Memo_v0.2_20261013_1643.md The memo should include: the selected project scope; the exact current-state canonical source set ; the broader desired-state evidence set ; exact versions/releases/commits/DOI archive versions/retrieval dates where relevant; high-confidence conclusions; answers requiring human review; source conflicts or missing information; inaccessible resources; important assumptions; difficult form/guidance questions; observations that may improve the workflow; representative data examples. 7.1 Representative examples in the memo The memo should include a small, diverse set of concrete examples: a few current-state examples directly from the selected canonical source; and a few broader desired-state/maximal examples when noncanonical project evidence reveals additional requirements. Represent examples as close to their source representation as practical: tabular/database source: show rows/tables using source column names where possible; JSON/YAML: show compact objects preserving source field names and nesting; RDF/graph: show triples/quads/edge properties; free text: show only the minimal excerpt needed; multi-source example: label it COMPOSITE/ILLUSTRATIVE ; record assembled across tables: label it DENORMALIZED and identify contributing tables. Do not fabricate values to create a complete-looking example. 7.2 Human review checklist Focus review on: Review question What to check Scope Did the agent use the selected project/data product and correct canonical source set? Current state Is every F1/current-state Y/M answer supported by the allowed canonical source set? Desired state Is every broader F2/desired-state Y/M answer supported by an allowed project source? Source traceability When F2 differs from F1, does Explanation / Considerations identify the supporting desired-state source and rationale? Claims Are the major kinds of assertions represented by the project captured? Evidence Are important evidence item categories and relationships represented? Interpretation Did the agent distinguish evidence from interpreted evidence, direction/strength, grouping, and higher-level synthesis? Provenance Are source, authorship, method, process, semantic alignment, encoding, retrieval, and other provenance requirements captured at the right level? Upstream EPC Did the agent avoid treating richer upstream content as current project representation? Intermediate artifacts If used for desired state, were they kept separate from current-state claims? Downstream enrichment Did the agent avoid treating API/UI enrichment as canonical current-state representation? Uncertainty Did it flag unsupported or ambiguous answers rather than guessing? Consistency Do responses across worksheets and the memo tell a coherent story? Examples Are current-state and desired-state examples accurate, sourced, and useful? Correct anything that does not accurately reflect the project. Once you are comfortable with the workbook, treat it as the confirmed project requirements input . 8. Step 5 — What happens after the forms are confirmed The confirmed workbook becomes the project requirements input for the later SEPIO requirements-to-model workflow. That later workflow uses: Confirmed Requirements Forms + Requirement→SEPIO Mapping Registry + SEPIO source schema ↓ Requirements-to-Model Output Package That package can include: Candidate SEPIO Covering Model Requirements Summary Requirements-to-Model Traceability Requirements Follow-Up & Modeling Decisions Gap & Extension Analysis Implementation Guidance Requirements Collection & Form Feedback Generation Manifest During the current AI-first pilot phase, an AI agent can generate these artifacts with transparent provenance. A future production workflow can move exact schema extraction, dependency closure, validation, traceability, and manifest generation into deterministic code. The project representative does not need to perform these mappings manually. 9. Evidence hierarchy and conflict handling A single global evidence hierarchy is no longer sufficient because current state and desired state intentionally use different source sets . For current-state answers The selected scope controls. Within the allowed current-state source set, prefer: explicitly designated canonical release/distribution; canonical schema/data model; canonical companion data dictionary/specification; representative records from the same release; other explicitly designated canonical companion artifacts. A noncanonical paper, intermediate artifact, or alternate distribution should not override current state. For desired-state answers Use the broader evidence set allowed by the selected scope. Prefer the strongest project-specific evidence, such as: explicit future requirements / approved roadmap / competency questions; current authoritative project/model documentation; existing project-maintained intermediate or alternate artifacts that demonstrate a capability; current curation/modeling guidance; current implementation/design documentation; older or historical project sources when they remain relevant and are not contradicted by authoritative current sources. When sources disagree: identify the conflict; state which source controls current state; state whether the conflicting resource may still inform desired state; do not silently reconcile them. 10. What project representatives are not expected to do Project representatives do not need to: learn the complete SEPIO model before filling out the forms; manually map project fields to SEPIO classes and slots; decide whether a SEPIO gap exists; design SEPIO extensions; understand dependency closure; or create the Candidate Covering Model themselves. Their responsibility is to help establish: a defensible scope; an accurate evidence base; and accurate project requirements . 11. Minimum evidence standard Before considering a requirements workbook ready for confirmation, the workflow should ideally have: a selected project scope statement; a clearly named current-state canonical source set; at least one authoritative structural source; representative examples from the canonical source; enough information to distinguish current project content from upstream/downstream information; one or more sources supporting desired-state requirements when F2 goes beyond F1; source/version information sufficient to reproduce the review; explicit review flags for questions the available evidence cannot answer. Projects lacking one or more of these can still participate, but the resulting workbook should contain more uncertainty/review flags. 12. Key principle The requirements process is requirements-first, not SEPIO-first . The project representative and agent should first answer: What does the selected canonical source currently represent, and what broader capabilities does project evidence support as desired requirements? Only after those requirements are reviewed should the SEPIO mapping workflow ask: How well does SEPIO represent those needs?
docs.title: SEPIO Requirements Collection — Project Representative Overview

docs.text: Audience: Project representatives who are asking an AI agent to complete the SEPIO Requirements Forms for their project
docs.title: SEPIO Requirements Collection — Project Representative Overview

docs.text: The SEPIO Requirements Forms describe what a biomedical knowledge project currently represents and what it should support about claims, evidence, interpretation, and provenance. The goal is not to redesign your project or force it into SEPIO while the forms are being completed. Instead, the process asks two related questions: Current state: What does the selected canonical source, dataset, distribution, or model actually represent now? Desired state: What broader capabilities does project-specific evidence support as requirements for a future SEPIO-based representation? This distinction is important. Current-state answers should be conservative and reproducible: they are grounded only in the canonical source set explicitly selected for the review. Desired-state answers may use a broader set of project evidence to identify a maximal, evidence-supported requirements set that a human reviewer can later refine or narrow. After the forms are reviewed and confirmed, a separate SEPIO requirements-to-model workflow can use them to: identify relevant SEPIO classes and attributes; generate a candidate project-specific SEPIO covering model; identify partial SEPIO coverage; identify model gaps or extension needs; generate implementation guidance; and identify questions requiring project or SEPIO modeler review. The completed forms are therefore a description of your project's requirements , not a list of SEPIO features you have chosen.

docs.text: At a high level: Define the scope. Decide what canonical source(s) control current-state answers and what broader evidence may inform desired-state requirements. Create a Resource Inventory. Identify the best sources, examples, versions, conflicts, access needs, and candidate scope statements. Give the agent the scope, inventory, forms, guidance, and needed resources; have it populate the Requirements Forms. Inspect the completed workbook and Requirements Review Memo. Resolve uncertainties and correct anything that does not accurately reflect the project. Move to SEPIO mapping. Once confirmed, use the requirements record as input to the separate requirements-to-model workflow. The remainder of this document explains each part in more detail.

docs.text: Before asking the requirements agent to populate the forms, define a project scope statement . Biomedical projects often have several related representations: an internal curation model; a canonical public distribution; intermediate curation or analysis artifacts; one or more source databases; an ingest/transformation pipeline; alternate or historical releases; an API representation; a knowledge-graph export; a user-interface representation. Without an explicit scope, an agent can easily mix these together and produce answers that are neither reproducible nor clearly interpretable. A useful scope statement identifies two evidence sets.
docs.title: 4. Step 1 — Define the project scope

docs.text: This is the exact source, dataset, distribution, release, schema, or explicitly designated companion artifact that controls the workbook's current-state / “Used in Current Data?” answers. The requirements agent should strictly use only this source set when populating current-state columns. Examples include: one versioned indications.xlsx distribution; one current LinkML schema release plus designated canonical example records; one KG release/export; one production database schema plus its canonical data dictionary. The fact that richer information exists elsewhere in the project does not make it part of current state unless the scope explicitly includes that resource in the canonical source set.
docs.title: 4.1 Current-state canonical source set

docs.text: This is the broader set of project-specific resources the agent is allowed to use when deciding what the future SEPIO-based representation should support. Depending on the selected scope, this can include: explicit future requirements or roadmap items; current papers and project documentation; model/design documentation; intermediate curation or analysis artifacts; information captured elsewhere in the project pipeline but dropped from the canonical export; alternate or earlier project distributions; competency questions; curation guidance; implementation/design documents. The desired-state evidence set supports a maximal but evidence-supported first-pass requirements record. “Maximal” does not mean speculative: every desired-state Y/M answer should still have project-specific support.
docs.title: 4.2 Desired-state evidence set

docs.text: The Resource Inventory workflow is designed to propose at least two reasonable scope choices.
docs.title: 4.3 Minimal versus maximal scope

docs.text: A minimal scope limits the review to one canonical source set. Example: Current-state canonical source: MeDIC matrix_indication_list.xlsx , version 1.3.0. Current-state and desired-state requirements should both be limited to information represented in this canonical distribution. This produces a conservative description of one concrete release.
docs.title: Minimal / canonical-distribution-only

docs.text: A maximal scope preserves a strict current-state source while allowing broader project evidence to inform desired state. Example: Current-state canonical source: MeDIC matrix_indication_list.xlsx , version 1.3.0. Current-state answers must be based only on this distribution. Desired-state evidence: additional MeDIC-maintained intermediate curation artifacts, alternate distributions, the MeDIC paper and project documentation, and explicit project requirements may be used to identify a broader, evidence-supported desired-state requirements set. Where desired state differs from current state, the supporting source must be named in Explanation / Considerations . This is often the preferred starting point because it gives a reproducible account of current representation while surfacing a broader set of requirements for human review.
docs.title: Maximal / canonical current state + broad desired state

docs.text: Some projects may justify additional alternatives, for example: current release + current pipeline artifacts; core product + designated companion datasets; domain-specific subset; strict historical release; current product family / multi-distribution scope. If substantially different products have different evidence/provenance behavior, separate requirements reviews may be clearer.
